claims.statement: `dispatch_agent_run` is the common agent/reviewer dispatch contract: it constructs or accepts structured `RunInput` and delegates to `create_durable_run`, which invokes `client.runs.create` with a caller-selectable multitask strategy that defaults to `"interrupt"`.

Durable dispatch defaults to `durability="sync"`, uses v3-compatible resumable/subgraph stream modes, and records an invocation identifier and start time while enabling the streaming compatibility marker; those settings preserve checkpoints and let dashboard clients replay externally created runs.

A completion webhook is attached to dispatched runs only when both `RUN_COMPLETE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is set and `COMPLETION_WEBHOOK_URL` is absolute and non-loopback; the receiving route rejects requests whose token fails verification.

Sandbox acquisition is thread-bound: it reuses a cached backend or reconnects through persisted sandbox metadata, and normal agent threads do not silently replace an unreachable sandbox because doing so could discard uncommitted work; deleted sandboxes may be replaced and reviewers may opt in to unreachable replacement.

Slack dispatch uses `multitask_strategy="interrupt"` for an explicitly tagged request and `"enqueue"` for an untagged follow-up, while a Slack message edit is put into the store message queue instead of creating a run.
Baby-sit terminal/failure updates and completed sandbox-background-task notifications use `multitask_strategy="enqueue"`, allowing interactive work to finish before their follow-up run starts.

The dashboard continuation path authorizes the sender and requires a busy thread, returning 409 for an idle thread and 502 when activity cannot be determined; it queues an attributed dashboard payload containing text, web surface, GitHub sender, and any non-text image blocks.

`queue_message_for_thread` stores `{"content": ...}` entries at `("queue", thread_id) / "pending_messages"` in FIFO order and caps the queue at 100 newest messages, dropping the oldest entries on overflow.
`check_message_queue_before_model` is a before-model middleware in both the agent and reviewer graphs, but the agent omits it in stop-summary mode.

Before each model call, the queue middleware consumes a batched autofix event into a system instruction, reads `pending_messages`, deletes that record before conversion to prevent duplicate injection, and returns a messages state update in queue order.

Queued messages are rebuilt through `build_input_messages`: ordinary blocks use `system:thread-queue`, dashboard payloads add a dashboard-handoff system message and an attributed web human message, and visible dynamic-context hashes prevent duplicate context while respecting summarization cutoffs.

The queue middleware resolves the thread model for image-url payloads, omits unsupported fetched images with a vision warning, and isolates errors so a model call continues; a failed queue read still flushes previously assembled content blocks.

A Slack `:x:` reaction resolves and validates its mapped Slack thread, requires and claims a unique event ID, cancels every pending/running run, clears queued messages and autofix events, marks the thread interrupted, and dispatches a stop-summary run mapped back to Slack.

A code-channel `agent_session_stopped` event cancels live runs, clears the same deferred records, marks the thread interrupted, and returns the Slack session to active without dispatching a summary run.

The authorized dashboard stop cancels all pending and running runs by enumerating the thread rather than trusting `latest_run_id`, marks it interrupted, and—unlike Slack stop—preserves queued messages and dispatches an empty-input continuation run when they exist; the admin variant does not perform queued continuation.

Run completion treats `error` and `timeout`, but not `interrupted`, as terminal failures; it posts a best-effort originating-channel failure reply with run-scoped idempotence, while successful eligible Slack runs schedule session-cost refresh.

Slack stop tests cover mapped and root reactions, cancellation of pending and running runs, deferred-work cleanup, summary dispatch, duplicate/missing-event safety, mismatch rejection, cleanup failures, and the no-summary session-stop path.
The background-task monitor claims a terminal task with a sandbox marker, records delivery only after the enqueue dispatch succeeds, and releases its claim on dispatch failure.
Structured queued payloads with the same `queue_id` are treated as already queued, making dashboard retry delivery idempotent.

Completion finalizes agent usage telemetry for terminal success, error, timeout, and interrupted runs when its payload has a usable invocation ID, and skips failure replies for automated `thread_wakeup` runs.
Successful non-automated agent runs schedule answer feedback, while Slack and code-channel status settlement waits until no pending or running run remains.
